text:
devon: We should build a new pulse/spike/tail generator for apples-to-apples kernel selection and batching experiments. Current replay harnesses don't separate KV-warm vs cold well and that skews p99s. Need deterministic seeds, configurable KV key reuse, and explicit burst shapes.

maria: 100% agree. My thought: 4 phases - warmup (steady low qps to populate KV), pulse bursts (short high-qps pulses that exercise batching), plateau (sustained medium qps), and long-tail dribble (very low qps with sparse large seqs). Keep them parameterized. :thumbsup:

ali: Proposed config prototype below. It must let us toggle KV reuse ratio and whether prefix cache is enabled so we can run with cache disabled for true apples-to-apples kernel perf. Also include a seed for request order.

ali: ```yaml
generator: pulse_spike_tail_v1
phases:
  - name: warmup
    duration_s: 60
    qps: 10
    kv_reuse: 0.9
  - name: micro_pulses
    pulses:
      - qps: 400
        width_ms: 500
        inter_pulse_ms: 2000
        count: 20
    kv_reuse: 0.6
  - name: plateau
    duration_s: 300
    qps: 50
    kv_reuse: 0.75
  - name: tail
    duration_s: 120
    qps_profile: exponential_decay
    kv_reuse: 0.3
seq_len_distribution:
  type: bimodal
  short: {mean: 32, prob: 0.8}
  long: {mean: 512, prob: 0.2}
enforce_determinism: true
seed: 12345
metrics: [latency_ms, batch_size, kernel_name, kv_hit, tokens_per_request]
```

jen: Nice. A couple of additions: - time_budget_ms and max_batch_tokens controls for batching heuristics; - ability to force token-aligned batching vs request-aligned for experiments; - instrument batch composition (num_reqs, token_counts) so we can see why kernels flip.

perf-bot: quick snapshot from last run with mixed kernels (aten_mha + fused_cuda) on similar load:

perf-bot: ```
p50: 11.3 ms  p95: 78.9 ms  p99: 234.1 ms  tail: 362.7 ms
batch_avg: 5.6 reqs / 420 tokens
kv_hitrate: 72%
kernel_select: fallback to aten_mha at high seq variance
notes: p99 spikes correlate with pulse edges
```

devon: Those notes are key. Kernel selection is nudged by batch token composition and by sequence heterogeneity during pulses. When a few very long seqs join a batch, kernels choose different execution paths and latency shoots up. We need test modes: 1) identical request shapes replay 2) shape-mixed pulses 3) cold-key flood to force low KV hitrate.

sre-ops: For reproducibility: pin model commit, python runtime, cuda driver, and run N=3 replicates. Use node labels to avoid multi-tenant noisy neighbors. TTL between replicates should be short enough to keep thermal state similar. Log kernel versions and kernel selection trace for each request.

ali: Question: how do we ensure apples-to-apples for batching heuristics? If one kernel benefits from slightly larger time_budget_ms, we must either standardize or sweep. I propose we run a small grid over time_budget_ms = [4,8,12] and max_batch_tokens = [1024,2048] and record best configs for each kernel, then compare pairwise at their optima and also at a standardized setting.

maria: Agreed. Also we should add KV-key lifecycle control: percentage of requests reusing hot keys vs new keys, and ability to pin a fraction of traffic to synthetic long prefixes so prefix cache warmup is measurable. That way we can report KV-warm vs KV-cold p99 deltas.

devon: Implementation plan: I'll extend the replay harness to accept the yaml above, add a plugin that emits per-batch instrumentation and kernel trace, and add a post-processing step that aligns runs by wall-clock phase boundaries so metrics are comparable. Output csv with run metadata for apples-to-apples join keys.

jen: Also add an option to inject a small number of adversarial long requests at pulse start to observe batch disruption. Keep seed control so it is deterministic.

perf-bot: Suggested acceptance criteria for a perf experiment: 1) reproducible p95/p99 within 5% across replicates for steady plateau 2) clear separation of results for kernel variants when config fixed 3) KV-hit vs KV-cold delta reported per percentile.

devon: Action items: ali -> wire up yaml parsing and seed control, maria -> define KV key pools and reuse patterns, jen -> add batch composition exporter, sre-ops -> test runner infra and node pinning. I'll prototype the generator this week and run a quick smoke test against the staging pool.

ali: On it. Will push a draft PR to eng-runtime/harness repo and tag you all.

maria: I'll drop a short checklist in the thread once KV pools are defined.

devon: Thanks everyone. If we can make this generator flexible it'll help investigate the kernel regressions we've been seeing and make comparisons much cleaner. :rocket:
